newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIAN SHARES TAKE BREATHER AFTER RECORDS.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIAN SHARES TAKE BREATHER AFTER RECORDS.

text.p: Leading Russian shares turned lower in morning trade on Friday despite a small rise at the opening, traders said, adding that the downward correction to continue in the short term.

The Russian Trading System 22-share index ticked up to open at a record 561.80 after closing on Thursday at a record 559.86. But slipping share prices were expected to nudge the index lower by the time it was next officially updated.
Dealers saw a three-day buying spree, which propelled stocks to consecutive record highs, starting to wind down.

"You can see a correction coming with the naked eye -- I think even the most adventurous buyers are starting to sober up a bit," said Creditanstalt Grant senior trader Andrei Galperin, adding the correction would be no more than five percent.
But he said high-liquidity shares were still well supported.
"The market will have an uneven rhythm today but it will not go down -- there is basically quite a lot of pretty aggressive money."

Oil company LUKoil LKOH.RTS slipped to $27.99 at 0915 GMT from its $28.02 closing on Thursday, while regional utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS eased to $1.721 from $1.760 and national power company UES EESR.RTS ticked down to $0.4584 from $0.4635.
Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkhikvadze said the market could close off Thursday's highs.

"People want to wait a little bit, look around, and maybe buy something a little bit cheaper after it comes down -- but none is going to drive it down indefinitely," Chkhikvadze said, adding he did not see support for current levels.

"We'll see what the West does but judging by the fall in ADRs yesterday, there might not be the support for the market that there was yesterday. In any case Russian demand for now is not holding the market up."
